service.name: Musicians for funerals, memorial services and celebrations of life
service.serviceType: A guitarist, pianist, singer or jazz duo for a funeral, a memorial service, a graveside and the celebration of life afterward
service.description: A solo guitarist, Spanish guitarist, pianist or singer for the prelude, the one song and the recessional at a funeral or memorial service, and a jazz duo or trio for the reception or celebration of life afterward, across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor, planned with the officiant or the funeral director and booked on short notice.

faqs.q: Can we hire a musician for a funeral on short notice?
faqs.a: Yes. A funeral is usually arranged inside a week, and a date that's a few days away is a normal request here. Send the date, the venue and the time of the service, and we'll answer against the booking calendar and come back with a recommendation and a price.

faqs.q: What music is played at a memorial service?
faqs.a: Usually a prelude as people arrive, one or two songs during the service, and music as everyone leaves: hymns, the standards, and the songs the person loved. Instrumental guitar or piano suits the service itself because it lets the words of a reading or a eulogy stand on their own, and a singer suits a family that wants a hymn or a song sung.

faqs.q: Do you play celebrations of life?
faqs.a: Yes, and that's where a duo comes in. Upright bass and guitar play the standards under the conversation at the reception, the restaurant, the club or the house, at 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, for an hour or two, and a singer with a guitar plays the songs the person loved. Where the family wants a jazz band, this is the place for it.

faqs.q: Can a musician play at the graveside?
faqs.a: Yes. A guitar plays a graveside or a scattering without power, on a battery-powered system or none at all, and the same guitarist can play the service before it. Cemeteries have their own rules about where a musician stands and whether amplification is allowed, and we ask them beforehand.

faqs.q: Can you learn a specific song for the service?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us the title and the musician learns it if it isn't already in the set, and the first learned song is included in every booking. Hymns, standards, folk and country songs, and the pop songs of the last sixty years are in the published song list on the repertoire page.

faqs.q: How much does a funeral musician cost?
faqs.a: We publish no prices of our own. What a solo musician or a duo costs in this market, with the sources, is on the pricing page. A service is priced as its own date, and a service and its reception together are one booking. Send the date and we'll come back with a recommendation and a price.
